title: Thundering token-routing: backpressure & graceful fallback hardening
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Follow-up work from the 2025-02-14 429 surge where a small set of routable tokens triggered a thundering-herd against a handful of gateway shards. This ticket focuses on hardening token routing, adding multi-tiered backpressure, and safe graceful fallback paths so a single misrouted or stale auth lease cannot cause cluster-wide 429 storms.
impact: During the event ~18:42–19:17 UTC, ~0.6% of live customer requests received 429s concentrated on gateway-eu-2 and gateway-us-west-1, affecting 27 high-traffic API keys (mostly mid-market customers). Observed client retries amplified the outage; downstream Dedicated pools experienced transient load spikes but did not failover cleanly.
timeline: 2025-02-14 18:39 UTC — first elevated 429s on gateway-eu-2. 18:45 — Ops routed traffic away from gateway-eu-2 shard-4. 18:52 — Partial rollback of recent auth-lease change. 19:03 — Temporary rate-smoothing rules applied; 19:17 — incident declared mitigated. 19:40 — initial RCA call and hypothesis formed.
root_cause: Combination of three issues: 1) token-router lease TTLs were extended from 10s→5m in a recent change leading to stale routing state after auth re-issuance; 2) quota-enforcer cache invalidation had a race when leases refreshed, causing tokens to be double-counted briefly; 3) the gateway lacked a second-tier backpressure circuit for per-token storms — requests were forwarded to Dedicated pools instead of gracefully throttling at the edge, amplifying load.
corrective_actions: ENG-42789-A: Short-term config rollback: revert token-router lease TTL to 10s (owner: Marco Li, ETA: 2025-02-16) — DONE
ENG-42789-B: Add per-token leaky-bucket in gateway edge with token-shaped decay (owner: Priya Patel, ETA: 2025-03-03) — In review
ENG-42789-C: Ensure quota-enforcer invalidation is ordered with auth lease refresh by adding monotonic lease id check (owner: Daniel Cho, ETA: 2025-03-05)
ENG-42789-D: Implement shard-local circuit-breaker and exponential backoff for retried requests to avoid cascade (owner: Marco Li, ETA: 2025-03-10)
ENG-42789-E: Add automated chaos test that rotates token leases and asserts routing convergence within 30s (owner: SRE Team, ETA: 2025-03-17)
ENG-42789-F: Dashboard & Alerting: New Grafana panel for per-token 5m QPS and alert if >X QPS concentrated on <1% tokens (owner: DataDog/SRE, ETA: 2025-03-03)
progress_updates: 2025-02-16: Marco reverted lease TTL change and deployed gateway-rollback-2025.02.16 (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/gateway/pull/2443). Immediate 429 rate dropped by ~70% in affected shards.
2025-02-20: Priya opened the per-token leaky-bucket proof-of-concept PR (https://github.com/redwood-inference/gateway/pull/2478). Unit tests added for token decay behavior.

2025-02-25: Daniel reproduced quota invalidation race in staging using scripted lease rotations; root-cause confirmed. Patch branch created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/quota-enforcer/pull/302
2025-03-01: SRE added temporary alert to detect >500 QPS concentrated on <0.5% tokens in a 60s window (playbook attached). Alert suppressed during controlled load tests.
2025-03-03: Circuit-breaker design doc reviewed with PM/Design; feature-flag plan approved. Implementation ticket created ENG-43012 for rollout orchestration.
notes: Decision: default to edge-side graceful throttling for tokens before forwarding; only forward when token passes edge admission checks.
Trade-off: tighter edge throttling can increase 429s for individual customers but prevents cluster-wide outages; will provide per-customer SLAs for Dedicated tier to opt into forwarding bypass.
Follow-ups: schedule a cross-team tabletop to validate playbook and SLO thresholds (owner: Ops Lead, ETA: 2025-03-12)
